title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
abstract: arXiv:2611.13254v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When an LLM agent fails part-way through a long task, the usual analysis records a symptom: a failure-mode label, or the agent and step judged responsible. It does not say where the error entered, which state carried it to the symptom, whether anything in the trajectory contradicted it, or which control could have caught it. We define an episode record that ties a candidate fault to its origin, propagation, detection, response and consequence, located by operational phase and state domain, and that names the control families whose observation and reach cover it. We turned the record into a written annotation protocol and applied it to 95 failed runs of six multi-agent systems from the public Who&When and MAD corpora, reading each trajectory in full. Faults enter early (median at 0.18 of the run), mostly as wrong decisions or fabrications over task state, and in 37 of 88 Who&When runs before the step the corpus' human labels mark as decis

translated_title: 可信赖的长时程LLM智能体：一项以轨迹为中心的实证研究——错误从何处进入、哪些控制手段能够触达它们
translated_abstract: 当LLM智能体在长任务中途失败时，通常的分析只记录一个症状：失败模式标签，或被判为责任方的智能体和步骤。这类分析并不会说明错误从何处进入、哪个状态将其传递到症状处、轨迹中是否存在与之矛盾的内容，或哪种控制手段本可以捕获该错误。我们定义了一种“事件记录”，它将候选故障与其起源、传播、检测、响应和后果关联起来，并按操作阶段和状态域进行定位，同时指明哪些控制类别的观察范围与触达能力能够覆盖该故障。我们将该记录转化为书面标注协议，并应用于公开的Who&When和MAD语料库中六个多智能体系统的95次失败运行，完整阅读了每条轨迹。研究发现：故障进入得很早（中位数为运行进程的0.18处），主要表现为错误决策或对任务状态的捏造，并且在88次Who&When运行中有37次的故障出现在语料库人工标注所标记的决定性失败步骤之前。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种将LLM智能体故障与起源、传播、检测、响应和后果相绑定的“事件记录”标注协议，并通过对六个多智能体系统95次失败运行的完整轨迹实证分析，发现故障多在任务早期（中位数0.18处）以错误决策或状态捏造的形式进入，且往往早于人工标注所认定的决定性失败步骤。
en_tdlr: This study introduces an episode-record annotation protocol that ties LLM agent faults to their origin, propagation, detection, response, and consequence, and through full-trajectory analysis of 95 failed runs across six multi-agent systems finds that faults typically enter early (median at 0.18 of the run), mostly as wrong decisions or fabrications, often before the step that human labels mark as decisive.
